cover.title: Professional AI Career Impact Report
cover.subtitle: How AI may affect your work, where it can assist, and where your human contribution remains important.

executiveSummary: Your work combines information tasks where AI may assist with responsibilities that depend on your own judgement and contact with people.
The sections below set out where assistance may help and where your contribution matters most.

measures.name: AI Exposure
measures.explanation: How much the work overlaps with characteristics AI can perform through digital systems.

measures.name: Human Advantage
measures.explanation: How strongly the work relies on human trust, context, physical presence, judgement and accountability.

measures.name: AI Complementarity
measures.explanation: How much scope there is for AI assistance while meaningful human contribution remains.

measures.name: Role Adaptability
measures.explanation: How much the structure of the role can accommodate technological change while retaining meaningful human contribution.

scoresTogether: Read together, your measures describe work with some scope for AI assistance alongside a clear need for your own judgement.

raising: Much of the work can be performed digitally
The work requires little physical-world presence
lowering: The work is less repetitive or standardised
The work depends on understanding complex or changing situations
Trust, persuasion or relationships matter to successful performance

safeguards.introduction: Keep these in place whenever AI assists with any part of your work.

items.title: Approved tools and confidentiality
items.guidance: Follow your employer's and profession's policies, and do not put confidential or personal information into tools that are not approved for it.

items.title: Human review
items.guidance: Review AI-assisted work yourself before it is used or shared.

items.title: Verify facts, figures and sources
items.guidance: Check facts, figures and sources in AI-assisted work against the originals.

plan.introduction: Three short phases, each building on the last. Work through the actions in order.
plan.narrative: Work through the three phases in order, keeping each step small and reviewed.

actions.title: Confirm your organisation's policy and approved tools before trying any AI assistance.
actions.rationale: Formal obligations or close oversight apply to parts of this work.
actions.reviewNote: Use only approved tools for any work-related information.
actions.note: Keep this step small and note what you learn.

actions.title: Map how you currently carry out “Investigate account problems” and “Update customer records”, noting which steps involve preparing, drafting, checking or organising information.
actions.rationale: These are the responsibilities with the clearest scope for AI assistance.
actions.note: Keep this step small and note what you learn.

actions.title: Write down what must always be checked or decided by you in those responsibilities.
actions.rationale: Assistance stays useful only where its limits are explicit.
actions.reviewNote: These responsibilities need close human oversight.
actions.note: Keep this step small and note what you learn.

actions.title: Note where “Communicate difficult decisions to customers” and “Respond to customer enquiries” depend on your judgement, relationships or presence, so any AI use stays around them.
actions.rationale: These are the responsibilities where your contribution matters most.
actions.note: Keep this step small and note what you learn.

actions.title: Try AI assistance on “Investigate account problems” for a few weeks, reviewing every output, and compare time, quality and errors with your usual approach.
actions.rationale: It is the highest-ranked opportunity with the least need for oversight, so a trial carries the least risk.
actions.reviewNote: Review every output before it is used.
actions.note: Keep this step small and note what you learn.

actions.title: Record where AI help was useful, where it was wrong and what you had to correct.
actions.rationale: Evidence from your own work decides what to keep.
actions.note: Keep this step small and note what you learn.

actions.title: Practise communication and relationship skills deliberately in “Respond to customer enquiries” and “Explain products and services”.
actions.rationale: Trust and communication are central to some of your responsibilities; continue strengthening them.
actions.note: Keep this step small and note what you learn.

actions.title: Keep what worked as a checklist or template, and stop anything that did not save time or protect quality.
actions.rationale: Only practice that proved useful should become routine.
actions.note: Keep this step small and note what you learn.

actions.title: Write down the safeguards you follow, such as review, approved tools and escalation, so they are repeatable.
actions.rationale: Parts of this work need strong safeguards.
actions.note: Keep this step small and note what you learn.

actions.title: Choose the next responsibility to try: “Update customer records”.
actions.rationale: It is the next-ranked opportunity in your analysis.
actions.reviewNote: This responsibility needs close human oversight.
actions.note: Keep this step small and note what you learn.

actions.title: Keep strengthening communication and relationship skills where your contribution matters most: “Communicate difficult decisions to customers” and “Respond to customer enquiries”.
actions.rationale: These responsibilities depend most on you.
actions.note: Keep this step small and note what you learn.

limitations: This report describes characteristics of the work you described. It does not assess you as a person.
It is not a prediction of job loss, and it does not forecast your career.
AI capabilities, and the way workplaces adopt them, keep changing.
The actual effect on your work depends on your organisation, the tools it approves, regulation and how changes are introduced.
Use these results to support your own judgement, not to replace it.
nextSteps: Use the 90-day plan, starting with the small, reviewed trial on “Investigate account problems”.
Keep human review in place for anything AI assists with, and follow your organisation's policies.
Look back at what you have learned at the end of the 90 days.
Revisit the assessment if your role or responsibilities change materially.
closingPerspective: Small, reviewed steps let you adapt your work in a practical way while keeping your judgement central.
